$comment: Modelog rate table. Base rates are USD per 1M tokens, transcribed from the published card. Every MULTIPLIER is an integer ratio over ratio_scale - never a decimal - because chained float multipliers produce artefacts at table-build time (3.0 * 0.1 = 0.30000000000000004). See PRD 8.2.
$schema_version_comment: Schema 3 adds the optional per-model long_context block. A model carrying one is priced by prompt length: a request whose INPUT-SIDE tokens (input + cache reads + cache writes - the card counts cache traffic toward the threshold) exceed threshold_tokens pays ratio/ratio_scale times every rate, output included, stacking multiplicatively with the modifiers table. Per the published card only Haiku 5.5 is priced this way; every other 4.6+ model includes the full 1M window at standard pricing.
$effective_date_comment: The OLDEST of this file's verification dates, by design: this field only drives a staleness check, and the original Anthropic entries (verified 2026-09-27) are the ones actually that old. Using a later date here would overstate how recently those entries were checked.
source: Anthropic first-party API list pricing (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, verified 2026-09-27; claude-haiku-5-5 incl. long-context tier verified 2026-10-12; claude-sonnet-5-5 verified 2026-10-15) and OpenAI first-party API list pricing (developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol, developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra, verified 2026-10-09; full table re-checked with no changes 2026-10-15)

cache_multipliers.$comment: Ratios over ratio_scale, applied to the model's base input rate. A model may override cache_read; the published card sets it per-model. cache_write_5m (1.25x) is also what OpenAI publishes for GPT-6 Astra ($12.50 vs $10.00 input) and GPT-6.1 Sol ($2.50 vs $2.00 input) cache writes - confirmed, not an accidental reuse of Anthropic's number. Codex's adapter always reports cache writes into the 5m bucket (OpenAI states no TTL tier), so cache_write_1h never applies to it.

modifiers.$comment: Request-level repricing, recorded per turn in message.usage. Ratios over ratio_scale, applied to EVERY token class. A value absent from these tables is UNKNOWN and must yield a null cost - see unknown_modifier_policy. Codex's service_tier shares this table under its own value names ("default", not "standard") rather than a separate field, since the role is identical: a request-level modifier the source reports per turn. Only "default" (confirmed against real captured sessions, ratio 1x) is listed. OpenAI's own pricing page shows every current GPT-6 model at uniform Batch/Flex=0.5x, Fast=2x, Ultrafast=6x of Standard - the ratios ARE confirmed and uniform across models, unlike this file's first guess assumed - but the exact wire value service_tier carries for those tiers has not been confirmed against a real Codex log (only "default" has), so turns on them correctly price as unavailable rather than guessed - see unknown_modifier_policy. Add batch/flex/fast/ultrafast entries here once a real log confirms the wire values.
modifiers.$service_tier_comment: Anthropic's own per-turn usage.service_tier (distinct from Codex's OpenAI tier, which rides in the speed table above). Only "standard" has been observed on real records (issue #12). The card's Batch API is a confirmed 0.5x, but the wire value this field would carry for a batched request is unconfirmed against a real log, so it is deliberately absent: a batch turn must price as unavailable, not at double its real cost.

$policy_note: An unrecognised model id OR an unrecognised modifier value must surface as 'cost unavailable' for that turn, never fall back to a default rate or a neutral ratio. A fast-mode turn priced at standard rates is a KNOWN model with a WRONG rate - the same confidently-wrong number the model policy exists to prevent, reached through a different door.
